audit_item_or_option: 1. SF Free Tenant Legal & Counseling Ecosystem
legal_authority: SF Admin Code § 37.9(c) (Prop F Tenant Right to Counsel for evictions via Eviction Defense Collaborative), MOHCD-funded Housing Rights Committee of SF, Bill Sorro Housing Program, Bay Area Legal Aid, and free Rent Board Petitions (Forms 516C & 518).
verified_value: Zero filing fee & no time limit on Form 516C rent-history audit
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: Assume every rent increase notice in 94122 will be reviewed line-by-line by HRCSF, BayLegal, or a Rent Board counselor/ALJ; even a minor defect voids the increase retroactively.

audit_item_or_option: 2. Rent Increase License Verification (Summary Petition Form 518)
legal_authority: SF Admin Code § 37.15 & Housing Inventory Rules: Tenant counsel immediately checks portal.sfrb.org to see whether the parcel held a valid license BEFORE the notice's effective date.
verified_value: Unlicensed increase = null & void ab initio
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: File Housing Inventory and archive PDF/screenshot proof of the active Rent Increase License for both units before serving any notice.

legal_authority: Rent Board ALJs strip out temporary passthroughs, fluctuating charges, and the $29.50 Rent Board fee, verify no rounding up occurred, and check that annual security deposit interest (4.2% in 2026–27) was paid/credited.
verified_value: Base rent x 0.016 exact cents + 4.2% deposit interest check
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: Pay or credit any accrued annual security deposit interest BEFORE or separately from serving a rent increase so there is zero offset counterclaim.

legal_authority: Cal. Civ. Code §§ 827 & 1954.53(d)(3); Rent Board Rules 6.14 & 6.15: Tenant counsel checks whether April 1, 2026 created a fixed term and confirms Tenant 1A's continuous occupancy bars any market reset.
verified_value: Original occupant continuity bars Costa-Hawkins reset
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: Treat Unit 1 strictly as a continuing rent-controlled tenancy at $3,995.00 base rent; wait until fixed-term expiry if the April 1, 2026 agreement is a 1-year lease.

legal_authority: Cal. Civ. Code § 1942.5 bars increasing rent within 180 days after a tenant complains of untenantability, requests code inspection, or exercises tenant rights; SF Admin Code § 37.10B imposes treble emotional distress damages + attorney's fees for bad-faith harassment.
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: Complete all pending maintenance requests promptly, confirm zero open DBI violations, and ensure at least 180 days of clean, non-adversarial repair history or fully documented routine anniversary scheduling.

legal_authority: SF Rent Board's 2025 Annual Buyout Report shows ZIP 94122 (Sunset) had 48 Pre-Buyout Declarations (#2 in SF) and 25 Buyout Agreements (tied #1 in SF), making Westside tenant advocates highly alert to constructive-eviction rent shocks.
verified_value: 48 buyout declarations / 25 buyouts in 94122 (#1–2 in SF)
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: Avoid sudden >10% banked shocks on long-term Unit 2 unless strictly necessary and fully ledger-verified; a standard 1.6% (+$50.40/mo) increase looks unmistakably like ordinary business administration, not displacement pressure.

section: One Unit vs. Both Units Analysis
audit_item_or_option: Protected Classes Across Federal / State / SF Law
legal_authority: Federal FHA (42 U.S.C. § 3604), CA FEHA (Gov. Code § 12955) & Unruh Act (Civ. Code § 51), and SF Police Code § 3304 prohibit differential rent terms based on race, color, religion, sex/gender/LGBTQ+, national origin, immigration/citizenship, primary language, age, disability, familial/marital status, source of income, veteran status, or height/weight.
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: In a 2-unit building, the other unit is an automatic 1-to-1 comparator; any unexplained single-unit increase risks a disparate-treatment inquiry if the two households differ in age, family status, national origin, disability, language, or income source.
official_source_label: U.S. DOJ — Fair Housing Act & CA Gov. Code § 12955

section: One Unit vs. Both Units Analysis
audit_item_or_option: Scenario A: Raising ONLY One Unit Without Objective Policy
legal_authority: Discretionary decision to raise Unit 2 (or Unit 1) alone while skipping an equally eligible second unit with no written, neutral rule.
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: NOT RECOMMENDED if both units are legally eligible: tenant counsel will immediately ask 'Why was only our client's unit targeted?' and probe protected traits or recent repair requests.
official_source_label: CA Civil Rights Dept. — Housing Discrimination

section: One Unit vs. Both Units Analysis
audit_item_or_option: Scenario B: Raising Unit 2 Now & Deferring Unit 1 Due to Objective Contract/Anniversary Gate
legal_authority: Unit 2 is month-to-month (since 2019 lease), whereas Unit 1 either (a) is in an unexpired April 1, 2026 fixed-term lease through March 31, 2027 or (b) has a February 1, 2027 24-month anniversary.
verified_value: Lawful & defensible IF tied to written building-wide rule
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: LAWFUL WHEN DOCUMENTED: Write a contemporaneous building policy memo stating BOTH units receive the standard SF Rent Board annual AGA on their first legally eligible periodic anniversary/lease-end date.

section: One Unit vs. Both Units Analysis
audit_item_or_option: Scenario C (Gold Standard): Uniform Building-Wide 1.6% Annual AGA Policy on Both Units
legal_authority: Apply the identical formula — current SF Rent Board annual AGA (1.6%: +$50.40 -> $3,200.40 on Unit 2; +$63.92 -> $4,058.92 on Unit 1 once periodic/eligible) — across both units on their respective eligible dates.
scrutiny_analysis_and_recommendation: STRONGEST PROTECTION AGAINST LAWSUITS OR INQUIRIES: Identical percentage rule (current 1.6% AGA), modest dollar impact, zero >10% shock, Unit 2's 11.5% banked balance preserved as unused reserve, and airtight objective neutrality.
official_source_label: U.S. DOJ — Fair Housing Act Overview
